usual_baseline: Six-monthly weight, pulse and blood pressure are the weak point, especially in adult CMHTs. Recording ranges from 8–19% [3198] to 57–84% [3262, 3622]; only 30.9% are monitored within NICE intervals [3622]. Some CAMHS and GP shared-care samples score 90–100% [3387, 3497, 3525]. Centiles are rarely used: BP 10%, HR 0% [3525].
fix_that_works: A dedicated ADHD clinic with a new initiation and shared-care process: annual BP 62.0% to 90.4%, weight 56.7% to 80.3%, longest wait 330 to 125 days (n=267 to 327) [3527]. A centralised caseload list and rating-scale retrieval: rating scales 3/7 to 6/7 [3482]. Presenting results raised weight 15% to 45%, HR 8% to 40%, BP 19% to 50% [3198].
fix_that_fails: Teaching and NICE posters did not move BP centiles (10% to 2%) or HR centiles (0% to 0%), because the electronic record cannot convert them [3525]. After presentation alone, Glasgow still missed NICE at 40–50% [3198]. In the clinic model, 6-monthly monitoring improved less than 12-monthly [3527].
consultant_advice: Most audits here are single-cycle snapshots of the same obs. The only large gain came from reorganising the service, not from teaching. Audit 6-monthly monitoring after a system change, or whether prescribing continues despite non-attendance, rather than repeating a baseline.
